takeaway: Supraspinatus initiates shoulder abduction (first 15°); deltoid takes over to 90°; trapezius and serratus anterior rotate the scapula beyond that.

question.text: Which of the following muscles initiates shoulder abduction?
question.say: Which of the following muscles initiates shoulder abduction?

lines.text: Picture abduction as a relay race.
The supraspinatus is the starter: it fires the gun and begins the movement.
It covers the first fifteen degrees.
Then the deltoid takes the baton and abducts the arm up to ninety degrees.
Beyond that, the trapezius and serratus anterior rotate the scapula for the last stretch.
And a painful middle arc points to supraspinatus tendinitis.
So the muscle that initiates abduction is the supraspinatus.
